question: Let \(N = 123456789101112\ldots4344\) be the \(79\)-digit number that is formed by writing the integers from \(1\) to \(44\) in order, one after the other. What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(45?\)
solution:
Because \(45=5\cdot9\) and \(5\) and \(9\) are relatively prime, we can work with divisibility by \(5\) and \(9\) separately.

To find the digit sum of \(N\), group the written integers as \(1\) through \(9\), \(10\) through \(19\), \(20\) through \(29\), and \(30\) through \(39\). Each group's units digits sum to \(45\). The tens digits contribute \(10(1+2+3)=60\). The remaining integers, \(40\) through \(44\), contribute five tens digits equal to \(4\) and units digits \(0,1,2,3,4\). Thus the full digit sum is
\[
4\cdot45+10(1+2+3)+5\cdot4+(0+1+2+3+4)
=180+60+20+10=270.
\]
Because \(10\equiv1\pmod{9}\), every decimal place value \(10^k\) is congruent to \(1\) modulo \(9\). Multiplying these place values by their corresponding digits and adding shows that \(N\) is congruent modulo \(9\) to its digit sum. Since \(270\) is divisible by \(9\), so is \(N\), and therefore so is \(N-9\).

Also, \(N\) ends in \(4\), so \(N-9\) ends in \(5\) and is divisible by \(5\). Being divisible by both \(5\) and \(9\), it is divisible by \(45\). Therefore \(N\) is \(9\) more than a multiple of \(45\). Since \(0\le9<45\), the remainder is \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
